// diagnostic

E0066

This function uses the retired effect-arrow spelling.

What

This function uses the retired effect-arrow spelling.

Why

Callable results use `->`, and an explicit effect ceiling uses the same unified arrow.

Fix

Replace it with `-[Effects]>`, or write `-[]>` for an empty effect ceiling.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0066: tests/ui/effect_arrow_retired.stderr.

Error [E0066]: this function uses the retired effect-arrow spelling
  --> tests/ui/effect_arrow_retired.jet:1:14
    |
  1 | fn old_set() #(FS) -> Int :: 1
    |              ^
 Why: callable results use `->`, and an explicit effect ceiling uses the same arrow
 Fix: write `-[Effects]>`; use `-[]>` for an explicit purity bound
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0066

Error [E0068]: this callable uses the retired result-arrow shape.
  --> tests/ui/effect_arrow_retired.jet:1:14
    |
  1 | fn old_set() #(FS) -> Int :: 1
    |              ^
 Why: a return type sits after the parameter list, and `->` introduces the body; an effect ceiling follows the return type
 Fix: write `fn name(...) Type -> body`, or `fn name(...) Type -[Effects]> { … }`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0068

Error [E0065]: this function uses the retired `::` body marker.
  --> tests/ui/effect_arrow_retired.jet:1:27
    |
  1 | fn old_set() #(FS) -> Int :: 1
    |                           ^^
 Why: A one-expression function body uses `->`; `::` binds a name, and `=` fills a slot inside a definition.
 Fix: replace `::` with `->`; `jet fmt` applies this fix.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0065
